elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement without consent to an affiliate.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no affiliate carve-out; an affiliate assignment that is not to a successor requires the other party's written consent.

elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement without consent to a successor in a merger.
elements.evidence: The right to assign to “a successor to its business” upon written notice permits assignment to a successor in a merger without consent.

elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement without consent to a successor in an acquisition.
elements.evidence: The right to assign to “a successor to its business” upon written notice encompasses a successor acquiring the Customer's business and does not require consent.

elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement without consent to a successor in a sale of substantially all assets.
elements.evidence: A purchaser succeeding to the Customer's business through a sale of substantially all assets falls within “a successor to its business,” for which only written notice is required.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign this Agreement without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause permits Vendor to assign to a successor to its business upon written notice, without Customer consent.

elements.element: Customer's consent to a Vendor assignment may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: For Vendor assignments requiring Customer consent, the rendered clause expressly states that consent “shall not be unreasonably withheld.”

elements.element: Vendor may never assign this Agreement to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: There is no competitor prohibition, and the successor carve-out could permit assignment to a Customer competitor without consent.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement due to Customer's change of control.
elements.evidence: The rendered operative language grants no termination right arising from Customer's change of control.

elements.element: Each party may assign this Agreement to a successor to its business without the other party's consent.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause states that either party may assign the Agreement to a successor to its business, with notice rather than consent.

elements.element: A party assigning this Agreement to a successor must provide written notice to the other party.
elements.evidence: Successor assignments are expressly permitted “upon written notice to the other party.”

elements.element: Any assignment other than an assignment to a successor requires the other party's consent.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause states that “any other assignment requires the other party's written consent.”

elements.element: Consent to an assignment other than an assignment to a successor may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause expressly provides that the required consent “shall not be unreasonably withheld.”

result.reason: The operative redline fully implements the fallback through a mutual successor-assignment right on written notice and a reasonableness-qualified consent requirement for other assignments. It does not meet the preferred position because it lacks an affiliate carve-out and competitor prohibition and permits Vendor successor assignments without Customer consent. Removing the overlapping assignment restriction from Section 3(c) is necessary to avoid conflict and leaves the unrelated restrictions on transfer, lease, export, and sublicensing of the Work intact. Drafting quality is reduced by ambiguity in “successor to its business” and by failing to specify when written notice must be given.
